input.title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via 'customer' query parameter
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:15-18: the route /orders/search (docstring line 17 says it serves the storefront's public order lookup page) reads `customer` straight from request.args with no validation. No authentication decorator or check is present (lines 15-22). main.py:20 puts it into the SQL string with an f-string inside single quotes: `... WHERE customer_email = '{customer}'`. main.py:21 runs it with conn.execute on a sqlite3 connection (app/db.py:8-11). A payload such as `customer=' OR '1'='1` returns every order (id, total, status) for every customer. A UNION SELECT payload could read other tables in the SQLite DB. sqlite3's execute() rejects multiple statements, so stacked queries are unlikely, but data disclosure alone is serious. The route is unauthenticated, so any internet user can reach it.
input.recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,)). Also think about whether a public lookup by email alone should expose orders at all, since knowing an email is enough to enumerate that customer's orders. Requiring an order number plus email, or authentication, would close that. Add a regression test that sends a quote/OR payload and expects zero rows.

input.title: False positive: /reports/status interpolates only allowlisted constant values
input.evidence: demo-store-api/app/main.py:28 reads the user-controlled `status` param into `key`. main.py:29 maps it through the REPORT_STATUSES dict (lines 8-12) with `.get(key, "OPEN")`, so `status` can only be one of the hardcoded constants "OPEN", "SHIPPED" or "REFUNDED". User input never reaches the f-string at main.py:31. Separately, the route has no authentication even though its docstring (line 27) says it is for the operations dashboard. That exposes aggregate order counts, but it is not SQL injection.
input.recommended_fix: No injection fix is required. For defense in depth and to quiet the scanner, switch to a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,)). Separately, check whether this internal dashboard endpoint should require authentication.

input.title: False positive: test seed data formatted into INSERT in unit test
input.evidence: demo-store-api/tests/test_search.py:13 builds an INSERT with an f-string, but the only values are the loop index `i` and entries from the hardcoded SEED_EMAILS constant (line 7). The function seed() is called only from the test at line 20, against a temporary SQLite file (lines 18-19). This test code is not part of the deployed app (main.py imports nothing from tests/), and no attacker-controlled input reaches it.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix needed. As optional hygiene, use a parameterized query: conn.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, 10.0, 'OPEN')", (i, email)). You could also exclude tests/ from this rule or suppress it there.

content.text:
I triaged the three scanner findings. One is a real, exploitable SQL injection; the other two are false positives. A draft ticket for each is saved and waiting for human review.

| ID | Location | Scanner severity | Verdict | My severity | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-001 | app/main.py:20 | high | **Exploitable** | **critical** | On the public `/orders/search` route, the `customer` value from the web request (line 18) goes straight into the SQL text inside quotes, with no login check. Sending `' OR '1'='1` returns every customer's orders. A `UNION SELECT` could read other tables in the database. |
| F-002 | app/main.py:31 | high | Not exploitable | none | The `status` value from the request is only used to look up a fixed list (lines 8–12, 29). The query can only ever get `OPEN`, `SHIPPED` or `REFUNDED`, so user input never reaches the SQL. |
| F-003 | tests/test_search.py:13 | high | Not exploitable | none | This is test setup code. It only uses a loop counter and a hard-coded list of emails (line 7). It isn't part of the deployed app and takes no outside input. |

**Fix F-001 first:** pass `customer` to the database as a separate parameter (`WHERE customer_email = ?`) instead of building it into the SQL text, and add a test that tries the injection. Even after that, anyone who knows a customer's email can see their orders, so the lookup may also need an order number or a login.

**Other notes:**
- I rated F-001 critical rather than the scanner's high because anyone on the internet can reach it without logging in, and it exposes data from other customers.
- `/reports/status` (F-002) has no login check either, although its description says it's for the operations dashboard. That's not an injection bug, but it's worth checking. Switching F-002 and F-003 to the same parameter style would be optional tidying.
